BayesianBenter

BayesianBenter provides closed-form Gibbs samplers for Bayesian inference in the Benter (1994) model for ranking data. The Benter model generalizes Plackett-Luce by adding stage-specific dampening exponents αr∈(0,1]\alpha_r \in (0, 1] that down-weight the information in later ranking stages:

p(πi∣λ,α)=∏r=1J−1λwirαr∑j∈Rirλjαr. p(\pi_i \mid \lambda, \alpha) = \prod_{r=1}^{J-1} \frac{\lambda_{w_{ir}}^{\alpha_r}}{\sum_{j \in R_{ir}} \lambda_j^{\alpha_r}}.

Estimation uses a positive-stable frailty data augmentation that restores conjugacy: the item worths λ\lambda are drawn exactly from Gamma full conditionals, and each dampening exponent αr\alpha_r is updated by Metropolis-Hastings on its collapsed conditional. Both complete and partial (top-RR) rankings are supported through a single entry point.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("pearce790/BayesianBenter")

Usage 

library(BayesianBenter)

set.seed(1)
lambda <- c(5, 3, 2, 1.5, 1)
lambda <- lambda / sum(lambda)
alpha  <- c(1, 0.8, 0.5, 0.3)

# simulate 500 complete rankings of J = 5 items
pi <- rBenter(500, lambda, alpha)

# fit the model
fit <- gibbsBenter(pi, J = 5, a = 1, b = 1, c = 1, d = 1,
                   iters = 3000, burnin = 0.5)

rbind(truth = lambda, posterior_mean = colMeans(fit$lambda))
rbind(truth = alpha,  posterior_mean = colMeans(fit$alpha))

Partial rankings are passed the same way: leave unranked positions as NA (or supply fewer than J columns) and gibbsBenter() routes them to the partial-ranking sampler automatically. Only the dampening parameters up to the deepest observed rank are estimated; the rest are returned as NA.

References

Benter, W. (1994). Computer-based horse race handicapping and wagering systems: A report. In Efficiency of Racetrack Betting Markets.

Pearce, M. (2026). Efficient Bayesian Inference for Benter Models on Ranked Data. arXiv:2608.23825.
